Chapter 5. Jesus and the Margins: Compassion for the Overlooked.
When you look at the stories of Jesus, you’ll notice something surprising. He’s never drawn to the powerful or the ones everyone admires. Instead, he moves toward those living on the edges—the outcasts, the ones who feel broken, the people others hardly even notice.
His compassion isn’t for those with perfect lives or spotless reputations. It’s for the folks who know, deep down, that they need help.
Imagine a woman, caught right in the middle of a scandal, surrounded by people ready to judge her. She braces herself for harsh words, but what she finds is mercy. Or think about a man whose life has fallen apart, someone his whole community avoids. Instead of getting pushed away, he meets kindness and understanding.
These moments show us what the heart of the gospel is really about: grace reaching out to the people who least expect it.
A lot of us grow up thinking that God’s love is only for the folks who seem to have it all together—the ones who check every box or never mess up. But the stories of Jesus flip that idea upside down. He goes out of his way to find the lost, the hurting, the ones who feel like they have nothing left to give but their need.
His life is a living example of radical grace—a kind of love that doesn’t stop at boundaries or social lines.
There’s something quietly powerful about being seen and loved when you feel invisible. The people who are weighed down by shame, the ones carrying regrets and feeling left out—those are the very ones Jesus moves toward.
The message couldn’t be clearer: No one is beyond the reach of grace.
So, what does this mean for communities of faith? Honestly, it’s easy to create groups where only certain people feel like they belong—where there’s an unspoken mold you have to fit. But if we’re really following the gospel, our arms have to be wide open. We’re called to make room at the edges, to welcome those who’ve been overlooked or left behind.
And here’s the thing: the ones most often ignored might just be the most ready to receive what grace has to offer.
